1.what: The Indecent Representation of Women (Prohibition) Act, 1986 may be called, extends to the whole of India and comes into force on a date determined by the Central Government.

2.what: This section defines key terms used in the Indecent Representation of Women (Prohibition) Act 1986: advertisement, distribution, indecent representation of women, label, and package. These terms are defined to help clarify their meanings for the purpose of enforcing the Act.

3.what: No person shall publish an advertisement with indecent representation of women in any form.

4.what: No person shall produce, sell, let to hire, distribute, circulate or send by post any book, pamphlet, paper, slide, film, writing, drawing, painting, photograph, representation or figure which contains indecent representation of women in any form.

5.what: A Gazetted Officer can enter and search places at reasonable times, seize prohibited materials, and examine records. No entry is made into a private dwelling house without a warrant.

6.what: Any person who breaks the rules mentioned in sections 3 or 4 can get: - Up to 2 years in prison and up to 2000 rupees as a fine. - If they break the rules again, they will have to spend at least 6 months in prison and pay a fine of at least 10000 rupees.

7.what: Offences committed by companies: Those in charge of company's business are guilty and liable, but may be exempt if they show lack of knowledge or due diligence.

8.what: An offence punishable under the Indecent Representation of Women (Prohibition) Act, 1986 is both bailable and cognizable.

9.what: The Central Government and state governments cannot be sued for actions taken in good faith while enforcing the act.

10.what: The Central Government may make rules to carry out the provisions of this Act
